title: Record the dispatch payload's location fields and the manifest's portable mode
action: Two unrelated files, both pure additions. In docs/knowledge/areas/advisor-protocol/slots-and-tiers.md R8 (dispatch payloads have one source of truth): when the unit's feature has a granted worktree, the payload also names where the work happens and where the coordination store lives, and the rendered worker prompt carries both - a worker in a worktree could otherwise not tell where it was; and a unit-execution dispatch names the agent that writes, not the read-only one. In docs/knowledge/areas/onboarding/release-identity-and-version-parity.md: the release inventory records each file's executable bit as version control carries it, not the raw permission bits the filesystem reports, because those are not comparable across machines - one platform synthesises a fixed value and cannot observe the bit at all, so a manifest written on one platform reported every record as drifted on the other; a checker that cannot observe the bit does not get to call it changed.

truths: R8 is extended with the location fields
the mode rule states why raw bits are not portable
